A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with HAD renamed HYPADE. The text, equations, tables, figures, and references support reliable comparison. v1 has no appendix; v2's Appendix A was included in the assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original six-dataset AUROC comparisons, pooling and centroid ablations, training-loss curves, and anomaly-score visualizations in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and reports additional HGNN comparisons and original synthetic-data experiments in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Despite the HAD-to-HYPADE renaming, Equations (1)-(6) and Algorithms 1-2 retain the same message passing, maxmin pooling, dynamic centroid, distance objective, and anomaly scoring. Newly supplied encoder and optimizer details do not establish a method redesign.

E1.justification: The six real-life datasets and their labeling rules are retained. Appendix A adds six inlier/anomaly combinations of uniformly sampled, similarity-based, and dissimilarity-based hyperedges, extending evaluation to controlled random, homophilic, and heterophilic associations.

E2.justification: v2 adds HGNN representations combined with the same one-class objective as an evaluated comparator in Tables 3 and 5. LSH, HashNWalk, VEM, and the renamed mean-pooling and fixed-centroid variants remain.

E3.justification: The original 80/20 inlier split, five-fold AUROC evaluation, and two-layer setting are retained. Added synthetic experiments specify 100-node, 3,000-hyperedge base graphs, 128-dimensional random features, and cosine-based candidate selection. Section 5.1 additionally reports maximum-epoch stopping without specifying the cap or establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix A extends the existing pooling and centroid ablations to synthetic conditions. New Figures 4-5 examine fixed versus dynamic centroid convergence and anomaly-score overlap, including differences associated with inlier sampling. The original ablation components and real-data analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports mean AUROC values only; v2 adds ± quantities throughout Tables 3 and 5. These quantities are not identified as standard deviations, standard errors, or confidence intervals. Five-fold averaging remains unchanged, with no reported increase in runs or new significance tests.

E6.justification: All retained real-data AUROC means match between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 3. v2 adds HGNN results and the synthetic results in Table 5: HYPADE scores 67.56-92.86%, while HYPADE-Fixed leads on Uni-Sim, 90.59% versus 89.60%. The stated Mushroom gain over VEM is also corrected from 27.95 to 27.96 percentage points.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)-(6) are retained, with no new theorem, proof, or derivation. The notation table restates existing definitions, and the added zero-weight collapse explanation elaborates the existing optimization motivation.

C1.justification: The claimed experimental contribution expands to include six synthetic datasets. The introduction narrows the training claim from requiring no labeled data to requiring no labeled anomalies, although the abstract and conclusion retain the broader wording. The central method and novelty claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that proxy class labels need not represent naturally occurring anomalies. It also expands the collapse explanation, interprets the HGNN comparison as supporting the proposed mechanisms, and links synthetic convergence and score overlap to the sampling conditions.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies PyTorch, fully connected ReLU encoders, 128- and 8-dimensional representations, Adam with learning rate 10^-4, and the oversampling target. Appendix A supplies synthetic-generation instructions. However, v2 removes v1's source-code availability statement and repository URL; this does not establish that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds NHP, Sun et al. (2005), Chen and Sun (2020), and dataset-source references, while dropping Kipf and Welling (2016). The overall positioning against earlier hypergraph learning and anomaly detection remains similar.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and method exposition are extensively rewritten and expanded. Graph and hypergraph anomaly detection receive separate related-work subsections, the flowchart explanation moves into the method narrative, and a structured synthetic-experiment appendix is added. Model names, author information, and publication headers also change.

P2.justification: v2 redraws and relocates Figure 1, adds a notation table and synthetic Tables 4-5 and Figures 4-5, and expands the main results table. Existing real-data plots are resized and relabeled within a new journal layout. Some left-column scatter panels are partially clipped in v2.

improvement.justification: The neural comparator and controlled synthetic cases strengthen evaluation of the unchanged method, while implementation details and the proxy-label limitation improve transparency. These gains are tempered by undefined ± quantities and removal of the code-access statement. Results are also incompletely integrated: Section 5.4 still calls VEM the strongest Mushroom baseline despite HGNN scoring 87.72% versus VEM's 72.04%.
